name: IoT, Embedded & Firmware Security
tagline: Reverse, emulate, and attack embedded devices in your lab: firmware extraction and boot-level emulation, UART/JTAG probing and flash dumping, side-channel and glitching rigs, RF protocol analysis (BLE/Zigbee/Z-Wave/MQTT), companion-app taping, and device databases.

tools.name: binwalk
tools.desc: Scans firmware blobs by magic signature and carves out embedded kernels, U-Boot images, squashfs/cramfs/JFFS2/ubifs filesystems, and config partitions, with entropy plots to spot encrypted or compressed regions.
tools.when: Every firmware image starts here: carve the filesystem out of the blob before anything else can be analyzed.

tools.name: firmware-mod-kit (FMK)
tools.desc: Extract-and-repack toolkit for router firmware (squashfs/cramfs/JFFS2); lets you patch binaries or files and rebuild a bootable vendor image. Largely unmaintained, so expect to fix toolchain issues before it works.
tools.when: When you actually need to modify and re-flash a vendor image (e.g. inject a telnetd) rather than merely read it.

tools.name: U-Boot Tools
tools.desc: Bootloader utilities (mkimage, dumpimage, fw_printenv, fw_setenv, mkenvimage) that inspect, unpack, and modify U-Boot FIT images and boot-environment blobs.
tools.when: Unpacking U-Boot FIT images, decoding kernel/dtb parts, or reading a target's boot environment from a flash dump.

tools.name: Firmwalker
tools.desc: Bash script that greps an extracted or mounted filesystem for secrets: shadow/passwd, SSL keys and certs, config files, admin/password keywords, dropbear/ssh artifacts, and URLs.
tools.when: Ten seconds after extraction, to surface default creds, key material, and backdoors before you read anything by hand.

tools.name: fwanalyzer
tools.desc: Filesystem audit tool from Cruise Automation that analyzes an extracted root filesystem image for setuid binaries, world-writable paths, insecure file modes, passwd-in-NSS, and other configuration smells, producing a custom report format.
tools.when: A structured, repeatable triage pass over an extracted filesystem instead of ad-hoc grep hunting.

tools.name: fwupd
tools.desc: Linux firmware-update framework (fwupdmgr/fwupdtool) that enumerates devices and applies signed firmware; in a lab it exposes device firmware versions, EFI capsules, and update/rollback flows on Linux-based research targets.
tools.when: Exercising a Linux target's firmware update path and enumerating what firmware components it reports.

tools.name: FirmAE
tools.desc: Fully-automated emulation framework (Firmadyne-derived) that uses arbitration heuristics to boot router/IP-camera firmware at ~79% success, exposing the web UI and SSH so you can fuzz and exploit it dynamically.
tools.when: Batch full-system dynamic analysis of Linux-based IoT firmware, on images Firmadyne-style boot failures block.

tools.name: Firmware Analysis Toolkit (FAT)
tools.desc: Attify's one-command wrapper around Firmadyne that boots Linux router firmware in QEMU without the PostgreSQL dependency; prints the emulated IP so you can reach its web server from the host.
tools.when: Quick, scripted boot of a single firmware image to poke its web UI and userland by hand.

tools.name: QEMU
tools.desc: Full-system and user-mode emulator covering ARM, MIPS, RISC-V, and more; boots extracted root filesystems end-to-end, and qemu-user builds run single cross-arch binaries, which every emulation framework sits on top of.
tools.when: The foundation of the whole emulation stack: boot a rootfs, or dynamically trace one bare-metalstripped binary before standing up full-stack tooling.
tools.install: sudo apt install qemu-system-arm qemu-system-mips qemu-user-static

categories.name: Hardware Debug Ports, Flash & Fault Injection

tools.name: PulseView / sigrok
tools.desc: Open-source logic-analyzer software stack with protocol decoders for UART, SPI, I2C, and 1-Wire; works with cheap 8/24-channel analyzers (Saleae clones, fx2lafw) as well as the Bus Pirate.
tools.when: Identifying unknown serial pads, decoding an unknown baud rate, and sniffing chip-to-chip buses on a target board you own.

tools.name: Saleae Logic 2
tools.desc: Polished commercial logic-analyzer software (free for low channel counts) with one-click UART/SPI/I2C decoding and robust triggering; pairs with genuine Logic 4/8/16 hardware or the popular HzKit clones.
tools.when: Fast, friendly decoding and decode-while-capturing when you have the hardware on the bench.

tools.name: Bus Pirate
tools.desc: Open-source serial multi-tool (current Bus Pirate 5): drives SPI/I2C/UART/1-Wire, reads SPI flash and EEPROMs, sniffs buses, and doubles as a low-speed logic analyzer and host adapter from any serial terminal.
tools.when: Talking directly to a chip over SPI/I2C, reading EEPROMs, or probing a bus before you break out a dedicated analyzer.

tools.name: minicom
tools.desc: The classic serial terminal for UART consoles at arbitrary baud rates; the everyday tool for reaching a bootloader, root shell, or firmware-upgrade prompt over the debug UART.
tools.when: UART pads or test points are exposed, and you want bootloader or shell access immediately.

tools.name: picocom
tools.desc: Lightweight, scriptable serial terminal with freshline handling and a minimal config; drops into non-interactive scripts, so it's ideal for logging UART sessions or pasting bootloader commands.
tools.when: Headless or scripted UART sessions where minicom's interactive menus get in the way.

tools.name: flashrom
tools.desc: Universal flash programmer with hundreds of supported chips and bus protocols (SPI, I2C, parallel, and via ch341a/mstarddc/ft2232 programmers); reads and writes BIOS, firmware, and SPI NOR chips with verification.
tools.when: Reading an on-board SPI flash out of circuit (or via clip) to obtain a full firmware image, or restoring one.

tools.name: CH341A SPI Programmer
tools.desc: Five-dollar USB SPI/I2C/parallel programmer (and its clones) that flashrom drives directly; the budget way to dump 25-series SPI flash with a SOIC-8 clip without desoldering.
tools.when: Cheap, disposable SPI reads on consumer hardware where you don't want to risk a J-Link or full probe.
tools.install: sudo apt install flashrom && use with ch341a_spi programmer

tools.name: OpenOCD
tools.desc: On-chip debugger for JTAG/SWD with a large catalog of CPU and flash targets, dozens of adapter drivers, and TCL scripting; halts CPUs, sets breakpoints, and reads back flash via the debug port.
tools.when: You found a JTAG/SWD header (or expose a testpad): OpenOCD plus a cheap probe gives you a debugger, and its flash readback doubles as a dump path for lockdown-immune devices.

tools.name: J-Link (SEGGER)
tools.desc: Commercial debug-probe family with polished SWD/JTAG software, flash loaders across thousands of microcontrollers, and RTT for fast printf-style logging from target firmware.
tools.when: A board already exposes a J-Link/SWD header, or you want a trouble-free flash-and-debug flow instead of fighting adapter quirks.
tools.install: commercial hardware + download J-Link Software pack from segger.com

tools.name: Pinecil
tools.desc: USB-C smart soldering iron with fast heat-up, excellent temperature control, and a huge tip selection; the go-to for tacking flywires onto UART pads, test points, and SOIC-8 clips.
tools.when: Practical lab work: soldering header pins, hooking UART/SPI flywires, and reattaching damaged pads before probing.
tools.install: hardware: order from pine64.com and power over 20V USB-C

tools.name: Hakko FR-301
tools.desc: Self-contained desoldering gun that cleanly removes through-hole components and chip pulls without collateral pad damage, invaluable for harvesting flash chips or isolating a faulted module.
tools.when: Removing a flash chip, connector, or BGA-adjacent through-hole part from a curious board without killing the board.
tools.install: hardware: FR-301 unit plus replacement nozzles

tools.name: ChipWhisperer
tools.desc: Open-source, open-hardware lab for power/EM side-channel analysis and voltage/clock glitching: capture power traces, run correlation power analysis to recover keys, and glitch to skip checks (CW-Lite, CW-Husky).
tools.when: Assessing a secure MCU's resistance to key extraction or fault injection on hardware you own, where the chip is the oracle.

tools.name: TrueRandom Debounce Adapter
tools.desc: Solder-free tag-connect breakout kit from TrueRandom that reroutes narrow-pitch debug headers (and exposes them) so you can desolder nothing, attack multiple boards in series, or chain a glitcher into the target.
tools.when: On small IoT modules whose debug adapters break off, or to insert a glitch/analog probe cleanly between connector and target.
tools.install: hardware: order the Debounce adapter set and clip onto the tag-connect header

tools.name: iotbreach
tools.desc: IoT/SCADA/embedded offensive framework — MQTT/CoAP/UPnP/Modbus/CAN/BLE/Zigbee/433MHz, firmware extraction, ICS kill-chain simulation.
tools.when: Testing embedded/IoT targets in your own lab.

tools.name: Z-Wave JS UI
tools.desc: Standalone web front-end (formerly Home Assistant's add-on) over node-zwave-js that pairs, configures, and interrogates Z-Wave devices through a USB stick, exposing command classes, values, and raw frames.
tools.when: Lab controller to inspect what a Z-Wave device advertises and to script device interactions while researching its behavior.

tools.name: Z-Wave JS
tools.desc: The core Node.js Z-Wave protocol stack powering Home Assistant and Z-Wave JS UI; parses command classes at a protocol level and is directly scriptable to send raw, non-standard frames to a device.
tools.when: Driving Z-Wave from code for fuzzing or deep protocol interrogation, or extending Home Assistant-based research setups.

tools.name: Killerbee
tools.desc: Python framework for 802.15.4/ZigBee security testing: scanning channels, sniffing and decrypting (default-link-key) traffic, and injecting/replaying frames with a supported radio (ATUSB/RZUSBstick).
tools.when: Live ZigBee interception and frame injection against Personal Area Networks in your own test environment.

tools.name: ZigDiggity
tools.desc: Bishop Fox's Zigbee pentest toolkit with a hardware setup around the RaspBee/Atmel RZUSBstick; ships attack scripts for insecure rejoins, ACK attacks, and lock identifier/enumeration against Zigbee home networks.
tools.when: Structured attack playbooks (beacon, scan, unlock, insecure-rejoin) beyond ad-hoc Killerbee usage.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/bishopfox/zigdiggity && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: zigbee2mqtt
tools.desc: Bridges off-the-shelf Zigbee adapters instead of vendor hubs so devices are attached and controlled over plain MQTT; exposes the individual clusters/eps of devices, ideal for observing how 'dumb' devices really communicate.
tools.when: Local lab network to enroll consumer Zigbee devices and drive them from MQTT while you capture and study their traffic.

tools.name: BetterCap (BLE modules)
tools.desc: Swiss-army network tool whose ble.recon/ble.sniff/ble.spam/ble.uart modules enumerate BLE devices, read/write GATT characteristics, sniff packets, and even drive a serial-over-BLE UART on a target.
tools.when: Rapid BLE recon, characteristic enumeration, and interactive testing of a wearable or smart device's GATT service.

tools.name: nRF Connect
tools.desc: Nordic's desktop/mobile app that scans BLE devices and browses GATT services, characteristics, and descriptors with clear D-Bus-ish tree views; the fastest way to map what a peripheral exposes.
tools.when: First look at a BLE device's services and charactistics before you script anything with a full toolchain.
tools.install: download nRF Connect for Desktop from nordicsemi.com (deb/AppImage)

tools.name: nRF Sniffer for Bluetooth LE
tools.desc: Wireshark plug-in plus nRF52840 dongle firmware that decodes BLE advertising and data channels, with RSSI trackers; the de facto way to observe full BLE link-layer traffic, including encrypted sessions for offline analysis.
tools.when: Capture-level BLE analysis (advertising, pairing, connection events) without modifying the target in any way.
tools.install: download nRF Sniffer for Bluetooth LE from nordicsemi.com and load .pcap into Wireshark

tools.name: mqtt-pwn
tools.desc: Akamai's Python toolchain (mqttez, mqtts-tv, mqttgama) that scans MQTT brokers, recovers credentials from device images, and lets you interact with topics (subscribe/inject) against smart devices running MQTT.
tools.when: Assessing an MQTT-enabled IoT fleet on a lab broker: credential hunting and topic-level injection.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/akamai/mqtt-pwn && pip install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: MQTT Explorer
tools.desc: Desktop broker browser that visualizes topics as a live tree structure with retain/retained values and history, making it trivial to spot insecure 'state' topics or mis-labeled sensor data.
tools.when: Grabbing a visual, real-time map of topics and retained payloads when investigating a live broker in the lab.

tools.name: MQTTX
tools.desc: Cross-platform MQTT client with scripting and a clean multi-connection UI; handy for pushing crafted payloads to topics and replaying captured values at scale.
tools.when: Scripted by-hand publishing/subscribing to MQTT topics during protocol testing of smart devices.

tools.name: tuya-convert
tools.desc: Jailbreaks firmware-locked Tuya IoT devices (wall switches, bulbs) by MITM-ing their provisioning phase and flashing an open firmware over the air, removing vendor-cloud dependency for lab control and re-flashing.
tools.when: Liberating a Tuya-based device from vendor cloud services so you can flash, control, and analyze it locally.

tools.name: Tasmota
tools.desc: Open-source firmware for ESP8266/ESP32 smart-home hardware that replaces vendor builds; its console exposes serial/MQTT/web interfaces and detailed logs that make a repurposed device an instrumented research target.
tools.when: Running a stable, instrumented firmware on a device you control, with full console and MQTT logging for traffic observation.
tools.install: flash release .bin with esptool or tuya-convert

tools.name: Frida
tools.desc: Dynamic instrumentation framework for Android/iOS that injects JS/TS hooks into a running companion app to trace crypto, dump secrets, bypass SSL pinning, and call internal APIs live.
tools.when: Tapping the device's companion app to observe cloud interactions, API calls, and key handling in real time.

tools.name: objection
tools.desc: Runtime mobile exploration toolkit built on Frida that patches APKs/IPAs, bypasses root, disables SSL pinning, and dumps the app's runtime state (keychains, class instances) without writing hooks by hand.
tools.when: Fast-win companion-app poking: unpin, dump keystore, and inspect the app's live memory before writing custom Frida scripts.

tools.name: jadx
tools.desc: Dex-to-Java decompiler with a GUI and CLI that turns a companion APK into readable source for static review of hardcoded creds, endpoints, and embedded SDK calls.
tools.when: Static pass over a companion app: find API keys, vendor-cloud endpoints, and logging before you attack the running app.

tools.name: Shodan
tools.desc: The internet-wide device search engine par excellence; query banners, ports, and products to catalog exposed routers, cameras, PLCs, and MQTT brokers, with Shodan CLI/scripts for pipelining results.
tools.when: Mapping exposure of a device model or product family (support/account required) before any lab testing against your own instances.

tools.name: Censys
tools.desc: Internet-wide scan and certificate transparency search (sweeping TLS/SSH/HTTP banners) that indexes devices by product string, useful for wide data pulls on banners and certificates for IoT gear.
tools.when: Banner/certificate-level device fingerprinting at scale, especially where Shodan's vantage set differs.

tools.name: cve-search (CIRCL)
tools.desc: Offline CVE database with Mongo/Elastic backends that correlates CVEs to vendors, products, and CPE strings, letting you answer 'what is known-bad for this router chipset' without touching the internet.
tools.when: Correlating a firmware version or chipset CPE against published CVEs during lab triage.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/cve-search/cve-search && cd cve-search && make

tools.name: NVD API
tools.desc: NIST's public REST API for the National Vulnerability Database; keyword-searchable CVE records with descriptions, CVSS, and affected configurations for quick lookups indexed by product.
tools.when: Direct, no-infra CVE lookups scoped to a product/CPE during a device assessment.

tools.name: Exploitee.rs
tools.desc: Wiki aggregating router/IoT hardware exploits, firmware analysis write-ups, and device-specific notes maintained by the community; excellent starting reference before you re-derive anything yourself.
tools.when: Looking up an existing method or exploit note for a specific router/device model during lab research.

tools.name: Proxmark3
tools.desc: The Swiss-army RFID/NFC research device (125 kHz + 13.56 MHz) covering low- and high-frequency tags, Mifare, iClass, HID, ISO14443/ISO15693, and EMV; use the actively maintained Iceman (RfidResearchGroup) firmware fork for sniff, clone, and direct attacks.
tools.when: Reading, sniffing, or cloning badges, keyfobs, and access-control cards you legitimately test, plus auditing a site's RFID exposure.

tools.name: libnfc
tools.desc: Low-level NFC library with CLI tools (nfc-list, nfc-mfclassic) that read, write, and clone ISO14443A tags through cheap USB readers like the ACR122U.
tools.when: Quick reads (UID, Mifare classic blocks) with a plain USB NFC reader before reaching for a full Proxmark3.
